biomarkers.name: MED12 mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common in phyllodes tumours and also seen in fibroadenomas; supports fibroepithelial neoplasm biology but is not solely diagnostic

biomarkers.name: TERT promoter mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Associated with progression/malignant behaviour; not specific in isolation

biomarkers.name: ER, PR, HER2
biomarkers.prevalence: Stromal component typically negative/non-contributory; epithelial component may retain ER/PR expression
biomarkers.clinical_use: Helps distinguish from conventional breast carcinoma biology; no established role for HR / HER2-targeted therapy in phyllodes tumour

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Biphasic fibroepithelial neoplasm with characteristic leaf-like intracanalicular projections and stromal hypercellularity
histomorphological_subtype.grading: WHO grading/classification: benign / borderline / malignant based on stromal cellularity, atypia, mitoses, overgrowth, and tumour border

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Not well characterised  dominated by stromal biology

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Stromal (mesenchymal) fibroblastic/periductal stromal cells of breast stroma; the epithelial component is benign entrapped mammary duct epithelium
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Mesoderm (stromal component) with entrapped ectoderm-derived mammary epithelium
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Biphasic  leaf-like intracanalicular growth of stromal cells around benign epithelium; grade determined by stromal cellularity, atypia, mitoses, borders, and stromal overgrowth
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Malignant phyllodes can develop heterologous sarcomatous differentiation (liposarcoma, chondrosarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma)  evidence of mesenchymal lineage plasticity in the stromal component
